briefing:
The Lumen Ridge flagship store launch is planned around a store opening on Wednesday 24 March 2027. The approved project budget is €260,000, and the steering group approved a reduction of €59,000 to the project budget in March. The shop-fitting contract is worth €57,500. Rising wage costs could affect the budget. The figure of €260,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Workstream ownership is settled. Joaquin Demir owns the shop fit-out workstream, Kwame Sørensen owns stock buying, Ingrid Szabo owns security, Yuki Kaur owns staff recruitment, and Rafael Achterberg owns the point-of-sale systems workstream.

The shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Thursday 25 February 2027. Working days for planning purposes are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening.

On staffing, the plan provides for 58 staff hires. An additional 2 staff hires were approved in March. Yuki Kaur's recruitment workstream covers this hiring, and the briefing material does not say anything further about how those two figures relate.

Stock loading can begin 3 working days after the shop fit-out ends. Kwame Sørensen's stock buying workstream is the one that connects to this step, so his updates are the place where the loading arrangements will be reported as they develop. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Several later milestones sit in the calendar after the opening. The marketing review is on Friday 30 July 2027, and the press preview is on Tuesday 14 September 2027. The fire-safety inspection is on Monday 22 November 2027, which falls within the security area that Ingrid Szabo owns. A delay in the signage permit could delay the store opening.

This note has been pulled together from the latest status updates and emails from the workstream owners. Figures and dates are quoted as they appear in those sources, and further detail will be added as each workstream reports in. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the number of staff hires.

briefing:
The Veridian sequencing lab setup is organised into five workstreams, each with a named owner. Rafael Oyelaran owns the facilities works workstream, and Kwame Esposito owns instrument purchasing. Teodor Achterberg owns LIMS configuration, Bastian Brennan owns staff hiring, and Idris Kaur owns cold-chain logistics.

On the schedule side, the facilities works is scheduled to end on Wednesday 3 March 2027. The first production sequencing run is planned for Wednesday 31 March 2027. Later in the year, the funder site visit is on Thursday 26 August 2027, the biosafety committee meeting is on Friday 19 November 2027, and the validation run is on Tuesday 23 November 2027. Late delivery of the freezer units could delay the first production sequencing run.

Instrument installation can begin 6 working days after the facilities works ends. For the purposes of that rule, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The status updates do not give a separate installation start date, so the rule is quoted here as it was stated. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the budget. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On budget, the approved project budget is $268,000. The steering group approved an increase of $23,000 to the project budget in March. The reagent supply contract is worth $34,000, and it is one of the commercial items sitting alongside the purchasing workstream's work on instruments. A delayed biosafety permit could delay the first production sequencing run. The figure of $268,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On capacity, the plan provides for 72 sequencing runs per month. An additional 4 sequencing runs per month were approved in March, the same month as the budget increase. The emails received so far do not describe how the additional runs relate to the planned monthly figure, so the two numbers are recorded here separately as they appeared in the updates. Reagent price increases could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

This briefing was compiled from the status updates and emails received to date. Each workstream owner remains the first point of contact for detail within their area, and the dates, amounts and counts above are copied as they were given in those sources.

The figure of $535,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The milestones further out are the first production sequencing run, planned for Friday 2 July 2027, and the validation run on Friday 19 November 2027. Priya, Kwame, Rafael, Mei and Idris each continue to report on their own workstreams through the regular status updates, and those updates are the source for the details above. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

briefing:
The Kestrel CRM migration has an approved project budget of $541,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of $18,000 to that budget. The vendor implementation contract is worth $28,000, and Zainab Novak owns the vendor management workstream, which covers the relationship with the vendor. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences. The figure of $541,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On the people side, the plan provides for 131 user licences, and an additional 6 user licences were approved in March. The trainer briefing is on Monday 8 March 2027. Aisling Okafor owns the data cleansing workstream, and the data migration is scheduled to end on Tuesday 9 March 2027.

Several other workstreams have named owners. Dmitri Castellanos owns the access control workstream, Joaquin Achterberg owns the integration testing workstream, and Emeka Iyer owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Each of these owners is the point of contact for questions in their own area, and updates from them feed into the regular project reporting. Licence price increases could affect the budget.

Testing follows the migration. User acceptance testing can begin 10 working days after the data migration ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The sequence therefore runs from the end of the migration through to the start of acceptance testing, with the integration testing workstream sitting alongside it under Joaquin Achterberg. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Governance and milestones continue through the year. The steering committee meeting is on Tuesday 1 June 2027, and the data-quality checkpoint is on Thursday 18 November 2027. The go-live of the new CRM is planned for Monday 29 November 2027. Aisling Okafor's data cleansing work and the checkpoint are closely connected, since the checkpoint concerns the quality of the data that the new CRM will hold when it goes live.

This briefing has been compiled from the latest status updates and emails, and it records the position as stated in those sources. Further detail on individual workstreams is held by the owners named above, and the figures and dates given here are reproduced as they appear in the project records. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

**Memo to Aisling Okafor, Programme Director**

**Summary**

The Kestrel flagship store launch is being run from the revised plan of Thursday 21 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. It sets the store opening for Friday 25 June 2027. Two risks could delay the opening: a shortfall in seasonal stock, and late delivery of the till system.

**Key facts**

- **Store opening:** Friday 25 June 2027. The email of Thursday 14 January 2027 gave Thursday 28 October 2027, but it is superseded.
- **Project budget after approved changes:** €227,000. This is the €249,000 first approved, less the €22,000 reduction approved in March. The proposed increase of €53,000 was rejected.
- **Shop fit-out owner:** Priya Marchetti. Zainab Nakamura supports the workstream.
- **Shop-fitting contract value:** €40,500.
- **Earliest stock loading:** Monday 31 May 2027. The shop fit-out ends on Wednesday 26 May 2027, and loading can begin 3 working days later.
- **Fire-safety inspection:** Wednesday 22 September 2027.
- **Security review:** Monday 27 September 2027, which is 15 working days after the stock buying checkpoint on Monday 6 September 2027.
- **Staff recruitment owner:** Marisol Quiroga. Corentin Esposito supports the workstream.
- **Latest marketing campaign sign-off:** Monday 15 February 2027. The point-of-sale systems kickoff is planned for Monday 22 February 2027 and can begin 5 working days after sign-off.

**Next steps**

Dated items and dependencies from the briefing:

- Marketing campaign sign-off completed by Monday 15 February 2027.
- Point-of-sale systems kickoff on Monday 22 February 2027.
- Staff training day on Wednesday 21 April 2027.
- Shop fit-out ends on Wednesday 26 May 2027.

- Store opening on Friday 25 June 2027.
- Stock buying checkpoint on Monday 6 September 2027.
- Fire-safety inspection on Wednesday 22 September 2027.
- Security review on Monday 27 September 2027.
- Press preview on Tuesday 9 November 2027.

briefing:
The Kestrel CRM migration has a planned go-live of Monday 29 November 2027. The plan provides for 269 user licences, and an additional 5 user licences were approved in March. The approved project budget is $292,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $44,000. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the budget. The figure of $292,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Workstream ownership has been assigned across the team. Idris Lindqvist owns the data cleansing workstream, while Yuki Brennan owns integration testing. Thandiwe Achterberg owns vendor management, Rohan Sørensen owns access control, and Lucía Quiroga owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences.

On the data side, the data migration is scheduled to end on Tuesday 9 February 2027. A data-quality checkpoint is set for Monday 6 September 2027, and it sits alongside the cleansing work that Idris Lindqvist is running.

The steering group approved an increase of $7,000 to the project budget in March. That approval came in the same month as the extra user licences mentioned above, so both changes were recorded at around the same point in the project's history. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

User acceptance testing can begin 10 working days after the data migration ends. For the purposes of that rule, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Yuki Brennan's integration testing workstream is the one that sits closest to this stage of the work. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Looking toward the end of the programme, the trainer briefing is on Wednesday 20 October 2027. The steering committee meeting follows on Friday 29 October 2027, and the go-live of the new CRM remains planned for Monday 29 November 2027. Thandiwe Achterberg continues to hold vendor management through this period, with Rohan Sørensen covering access control and Lucía Quiroga covering the reporting dashboards. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences.

Thandiwe Achterberg continues to hold vendor management through this period, with Rohan Sørensen covering access control and Lucía Quiroga covering the reporting dashboards. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

briefing:
The Granitefold sequencing lab setup is organised around five workstreams, each with a named owner. Amara Petrov owns the facilities works workstream, Rafael Mwangi owns instrument purchasing, and Leilani Bakshi owns biosafety approval. Noor Novak owns staff hiring, while Idris Valdés owns cold-chain logistics. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is $171,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of $53,000 to the project budget. The reagent supply contract is worth $74,000. A budget review is set for Wednesday 13 October 2027, and it will be the next formal point at which these figures are looked at together. Late delivery of the freezer units could delay the first production sequencing run. The figure of $171,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The facilities works is scheduled to end on Friday 4 June 2027. The validation run follows shortly after, on Tuesday 8 June 2027, and the biosafety committee meets on Tuesday 15 June 2027. Leilani Bakshi's workstream is the one connected to that committee meeting. Reagent price increases could affect the budget.

Instrument installation can begin 5 working days after the facilities works ends. For the purposes of this calculation, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Rafael Mwangi's purchasing workstream supplies the instruments that this installation step relies on. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Looking toward operations, the first production sequencing run is planned for Monday 16 August 2027. The plan provides for 68 sequencing runs per month. In March, an additional 8 sequencing runs per month were approved, and that approval sits alongside the existing plan figure as reported in the updates. Idris Valdés's cold-chain logistics work and Noor Novak's hiring work both feed into running at that level once production starts. A delayed biosafety permit could delay the first production sequencing run.

This briefing draws only on the status updates and emails received so far. Further detail on each workstream can come from its owner, and the budget review in October is the scheduled checkpoint for the financial position.

The Tidewell warehouse automation plan provides for 20 picking robots, and the switch to automated picking is planned for Wednesday 27 October 2027. Workstream ownership has been settled, and the notes below follow the people behind each piece of work as well as the dates that matter in the coming months.

On the schedule, the safety committee meets on Tuesday 2 February 2027. The supplier factory visit follows on Wednesday 17 February 2027, and the insurance assessment is on Friday 19 February 2027. All three fall before the floor reinforcement work is due to finish.

Dmitri Haddad owns the safety training workstream, which is the natural counterpart to the safety committee meeting. Priya Sørensen owns the software integration workstream, and Leilani Nakamura owns the maintenance contracts workstream. The maintenance contract is worth €80,500. Union consultation on shift patterns could affect the budget.

On budget, the approved project budget is €527,000. The steering group approved a reduction of €33,000 to the project budget in March, in the same month as the approval of the additional picking robots. The figures are reported here as they appear in the status updates and emails received so far. A failed load test on the mezzanine could delay the switch to automated picking. The figure of €527,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On delegate capacity, the plan provides for 688 delegate places. An additional 18 delegate places were approved in March. Both items are reported as they appear in the source updates, and this note does not combine them into a single figure. Late venue licensing could delay the conference opening day.

The date itself has not been stated in any of the status updates, so it is left as the rule is written. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Several workstreams are owned by other colleagues. Bastian Novak owns the catering workstream, and the catering tasting is on Thursday 14 October 2027. Freya Quiroga owns the sponsorship workstream, which is reported separately from the venue and production items. Further updates from each workstream owner will be added to this briefing as they arrive, and the dates and amounts above are quoted exactly as they appear in the emails and status reports received to date. briefing:
Brightwater Eastside clinic opening: project briefing Low early patient uptake could affect the number of treatment chairs.

Pulling together the latest status updates and emails, the approved project budget stands at €367,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of €9,000 to the project budget. The imaging equipment lease is worth €23,000, and that sits alongside the rest of the spending picture without any further adjustment noted here. Late delivery of the X-ray unit could delay the first day of patient appointments. The figure of €367,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On ownership, Emeka Quiroga owns the building fit-out workstream, and the fit-out is scheduled to end on Wednesday 3 February 2027. Leilani Iyer owns the clinical staffing workstream, while Zainab Marchetti owns the community outreach workstream. Bastian Takahashi owns the patient records workstream, and Teodor Castellanos owns the regulatory approval workstream.

On the physical side, the plan provides for 33 treatment chairs. An additional 5 treatment chairs were approved in March, and the updates I have seen do not say how those sit against the original plan. Equipment installation can begin 6 working days after the building fit-out ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Unfilled nurse vacancies could delay the first day of patient appointments. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Looking at the calendar, the staff induction day is on Wednesday 31 March 2027. The first day of patient appointments is planned for Wednesday 2 June 2027. The governance board meeting follows on Tuesday 29 June 2027, and the pharmacy stock delivery is on Thursday 18 November 2027. Higher energy tariffs could affect the budget.

That is the position as it stands in the status updates and emails received so far. Each workstream has a named owner, and the budget, chair, equipment and scheduling points above are recorded as they were reported. Any further detail will be added to this briefing as new updates arrive from the workstream owners.

reference:
**Memo to: Oluwaseun Szabo, Programme Director**
**Re: Marrowfield flagship store launch**

**Summary**

The store opening is currently Tuesday 3 August 2027, as set by the revised plan of Thursday 28 January 2027. That plan supersedes the earlier email of 5 January 2027, which gave 21 October 2027. Two risks could delay the opening: a delay in the signage permit, and late delivery of the till system.

**Key facts**

- Earliest date stock loading can begin: Monday 1 March 2027, which is 4 working days after the shop fit-out ends on Tuesday 23 February 2027.
- Latest date for marketing campaign sign-off, for the shop fit-out kickoff to go ahead on its planned date of Wednesday 1 September 2027: Friday 20 August 2027. The kickoff can begin 8 working days after sign-off.
- The stock buying review on Wednesday 2 June 2027 takes place 6 working days after the staff recruitment checkpoint on Tuesday 25 May 2027.
- The fire-safety inspection is on Monday 18 October 2027.
- Teodor Okafor owns the security workstream.
- Corentin Oyelaran owns the point-of-sale systems workstream.
- The project budget after all approved changes is €437,000. This is the €443,000 first approved, less the €6,000 reduction approved in March. The proposed further increase of €11,000 was rejected.
- The shop-fitting contract is worth €43,000.

**Next steps**

- Shop fit-out ends on Tuesday 23 February 2027, and stock loading can begin 4 working days later.
- The staff recruitment checkpoint is on Tuesday 25 May 2027.
- The stock buying review is on Wednesday 2 June 2027.
- The stock count is on Thursday 22 July 2027.
- The store opens on Tuesday 3 August 2027.
- The shop fit-out kickoff is planned for Wednesday 1 September 2027 and depends on marketing campaign sign-off being completed by Friday 20 August 2027.
- The staff training day is on Friday 27 August 2027.
- The fire-safety inspection is on Monday 18 October 2027.

Oluwaseun Achterberg owns the network cabling workstream, Yuki Mensah owns the security badges workstream, and Sanna Novak owns the furniture procurement workstream. Hamid Valdés owns the staff communications workstream, and Lucía Kaur owns the moving logistics workstream. A delay in fire-safety certification could delay the official opening of the new office.

Higher-than-expected furniture prices could affect the budget. The figure of £228,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The plan provides for 198 desks. An additional 11 desks were approved in March, at the same point in the project as the budget increase. Furniture delivery is on Wednesday 1 September 2027, which falls the day after the official opening of the new office, planned for Tuesday 31 August 2027.

**Memo to Svetlana Quiroga, Programme Director**

**Summary**

The switch to automated picking is now set for Thursday 14 October 2027, under the revised plan of Friday 22 January 2027. That plan supersedes all earlier emails, including the one of 5 January 2027 that gave 15 July 2027. Two risks could delay the switch: a failed load test on the mezzanine, and delayed customs clearance for the robots.

**Key facts**

- Project budget after all approved changes: €215,000. This is the €169,000 first approved plus the €46,000 increase approved in March. The further proposed increase of €37,000 was rejected.
- Maintenance contract value: €27,000.
- Earliest date robot installation can begin: Thursday 25 March 2027, which is 5 working days after floor reinforcement ends on Thursday 18 March 2027.
- The safety training review on Friday 23 July 2027 takes place 20 working days after the robot procurement checkpoint on Friday 25 June 2027.
- The operator training course is on Monday 30 August 2027.
- The latest date for software integration sign-off, for the maintenance contracts kickoff to go ahead on its planned date of Friday 26 February 2027, is Monday 22 February 2027.
- Corentin Okafor owns the shift planning workstream.
- Oluwaseun Esposito owns the floor reinforcement workstream.

Dated items and dependencies from the briefing:

- Software integration sign-off by Monday 22 February 2027.
- Maintenance contracts kickoff on Friday 26 February 2027.
- Insurance assessment on Tuesday 6 April 2027.
- Robot procurement checkpoint on Friday 25 June 2027.
- Safety training review on Friday 23 July 2027.
- Operator training course on Monday 30 August 2027.
- Switch to automated picking on Thursday 14 October 2027.
- Safety committee meeting on Tuesday 26 October 2027.

briefing:
The Veridian flagship store launch is progressing across several workstreams, each with a named owner. Tomasz Esposito owns the shop fit-out workstream, Priya Mensah owns the stock buying workstream, Rafael Achterberg owns the staff recruitment workstream, Corentin Delacroix owns the marketing campaign workstream, and Yuki Petrov owns the point-of-sale systems workstream. Updates from each of them have fed into this summary.

On the money side, the approved project budget is €400,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of €56,000 to the project budget. Separately, the shop-fitting contract is worth €44,500. The sources do not say anything further about how these figures relate to one another, and this briefing does not attempt to reconcile them. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the budget. The figure of €400,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Thursday 13 May 2027. That milestone sits at the front of the construction sequence and drives the stock timetable that follows it. Tomasz Esposito's workstream is the one responsible for delivering it, and the fit-out contract is the one referred to above. A shortfall in seasonal stock could delay the store opening.

Stock loading can begin 4 working days after the shop fit-out ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The stock count is on Monday 31 May 2027, and Priya Mensah's stock buying workstream sits alongside both of these stock-related steps. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On people, the plan provides for 69 staff hires. An additional 9 staff hires were approved in March, in the same month as the budget increase. Rafael Achterberg's recruitment workstream covers hiring, and the staff training day is on Wednesday 15 September 2027, which is the scheduled point for bringing the team together before the store opens. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the number of staff hires.

Marketing and launch events are the remaining items. The press preview is on Tuesday 15 June 2027, and Corentin Delacroix's marketing campaign workstream is the natural home for that event. The store opening is planned for Tuesday 26 October 2027. Yuki Petrov's point-of-sale systems workstream completes the set of owned areas, and no further detail on that workstream has been provided in the updates received so far. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening.

briefing:
The Ostrava Eastside clinic opening is being coordinated across five workstreams, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails. Tomasz Esposito owns the building fit-out workstream, which is scheduled to end on Wednesday 3 February 2027. Kwame Demir owns equipment procurement, while Leilani Quiroga owns clinical staffing.

On the community side, Yuki Delacroix owns the outreach workstream. The open evening for residents is on Wednesday 17 February 2027, and it is the main outreach event currently in the plan. Bastian Takahashi owns the patient records workstream, which sits alongside the other four and supports the same opening.

On budget, the approved project budget is €493,000. The steering group approved an increase of €57,000 to the project budget in March. Separately, the imaging equipment lease is worth €84,500. Higher energy tariffs could affect the budget. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Further updates will be added to this briefing as the workstream owners send them in, with each owner remaining the point of contact for their own area. A rise in insurance premiums could affect the number of treatment chairs.

reference:
**Memo to Anders Kaur, Programme Director**

**Summary**

This memo covers the Fernhollow warehouse automation, which is governed by the revised plan of Monday 25 January 2027. That plan supersedes all earlier emails. The switch to automated picking is now Monday 25 October 2027. The earlier date of Thursday 1 July 2027 no longer applies.

**Key facts**

- Switch to automated picking: Monday 25 October 2027.
- Risks that could delay the switch: late delivery of charging stations, and delayed customs clearance for the robots.
- Project budget after all approved changes: €381,000. This is the €388,000 first approved, less the €7,000 reduction approved in March. The proposed increase of €38,000 was rejected.
- Maintenance contract value: €14,500.
- Safety committee meeting: Thursday 22 July 2027.
- Software integration workstream owner: Leilani Demir.
- Safety training workstream owner: Hamid Lindqvist.
- Shift planning review: Monday 19 April 2027, which is 9 working days after the floor reinforcement checkpoint on Tuesday 6 April 2027.
- Earliest robot installation start: Thursday 10 June 2027, which is 10 working days after floor reinforcement ends on Thursday 27 May 2027.
- Latest maintenance contracts sign-off for the robot procurement kickoff to go ahead as planned: Monday 15 February 2027. The kickoff is Monday 22 February 2027 and needs 5 working days after sign-off.

**Next steps**

- Robot procurement kickoff: Monday 22 February 2027, dependent on maintenance contracts sign-off by Monday 15 February 2027.
- Shift planning review: Monday 19 April 2027.
- Floor reinforcement work ends Thursday 27 May 2027, after which robot installation can begin 10 working days later.
- Supplier factory visit: Monday 21 June 2027.
- Safety committee meeting: Thursday 22 July 2027.
- Operator training course: Monday 18 October 2027.
- Switch to automated picking: Monday 25 October 2027.

Corentin Marchetti owns the facilities works workstream, and the facilities works is scheduled to end on Thursday 17 June 2027. The approved project budget is $548,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of $35,000 to the project budget, and the same month an additional 10 sequencing runs per month were approved. The plan provides for 57 sequencing runs per month. The figure of $548,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Aisling Takahashi owns the biosafety approval workstream. The biosafety committee meeting is on Friday 7 May 2027, which is the point at which that workstream's approval matters are taken up by the committee. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the budget.

On the instrument side, instrument installation can begin 8 working days after the facilities works ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The validation run is on Wednesday 23 June 2027. A delayed biosafety permit could delay the first production sequencing run. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Marisol Quiroga owns the LIMS configuration workstream, while Anders Abernethy owns the cold-chain logistics workstream. The reagent supply contract is worth $79,500. Thandiwe Valdés owns the staff hiring workstream. An unfilled lab manager post could delay the first production sequencing run.

Looking further ahead, the vendor training week is on Thursday 11 November 2027. The first production sequencing run is planned for Friday 8 October 2027. Both of those entries appear in the schedule alongside the earlier milestones, and the workstream owners named above are the contacts for their respective areas as the lab setup at Fernhollow proceeds.

The budget and run-rate figures come from the March steering group decisions and the current plan, and the contract value comes from the reagent supply agreement. The dates quoted are those currently in the schedule for the Fernhollow sequencing lab. Reagent price increases could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

briefing:
The Granitefold flagship store opening is planned for Wednesday 21 April 2027, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails on the launch. The approved project budget is €256,000. In March, the steering group approved a reduction of €32,000 to the project budget, and the figures above are quoted as they appear in the source material. Rising wage costs could affect the number of staff hires. The figure of €256,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On the physical build, the shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Monday 1 March 2027. The shop-fitting contract is worth €70,500. The stock count follows shortly afterwards, on Wednesday 3 March 2027, and it is the next fixed date on the stock side of the plan. A delay in the signage permit could delay the store opening.

Stock loading can begin 8 working days after the shop fit-out ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Bastian Novak owns the stock buying workstream, so questions about what is being bought and when it arrives sit with him. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

People and systems are covered by several named owners. Ingrid Whitfield owns the staff recruitment workstream. The plan provides for 51 staff hires, and an additional 8 staff hires were approved in March. Yuki Marchetti owns the point-of-sale systems workstream, while Svetlana Kaur owns the security workstream. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the budget.

Marketing is led by Elif Kowalczyk, who owns the marketing campaign workstream. The press preview is on Tuesday 6 April 2027, ahead of the opening on Wednesday 21 April 2027. A marketing review is set for Wednesday 10 November 2027, which falls well after the store has opened.

To summarise the ownership picture, each of the five workstreams named above has a single owner: stock buying, staff recruitment, point-of-sale systems, security and the marketing campaign. The dates in this note are those currently recorded in the status updates and emails, and the budget and hiring decisions made in March are included as they were reported. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening.

briefing:
The Tidewell office relocation has several workstreams under way, each with a named owner. Elif Brennan owns the lease negotiation workstream, and Teodor Whitfield owns furniture procurement. Idris Nakamura owns the network cabling workstream, Emeka Kaur owns security badges, and Thandiwe Oyelaran owns moving logistics. Higher-than-expected furniture prices could affect the number of desks.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is £445,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of £18,000 to the project budget. Separately, the furniture supplier contract is worth £57,000. These figures are reported as they appear in the status updates, without any reconciliation between them. A shortage of parking spaces could affect the budget. The figure of £445,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The plan provides for 135 desks. An additional 9 desks were approved in March, in the same month as the budget increase. The updates do not say how the additional desks relate to the plan figure, so the two are recorded here as stated. A delay in fire-safety certification could delay the official opening of the new office.

On the technical schedule, the network cabling installation is scheduled to end on Friday 12 March 2027. Idris Nakamura's workstream carries that milestone, and other activity in the building follows from it. A dispute over the lift installation could delay the official opening of the new office.

The staff move-in can begin 6 working days after the network cabling installation ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. That rule is recorded as written, and the move-in sits within the area covered by Thandiwe Oyelaran's logistics workstream. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

The official opening of the new office is planned for Monday 12 April 2027. Later in the year, the calendar holds several fixed events. The security audit is on Tuesday 15 June 2027, which falls within the scope of the security badges work led by Emeka Kaur. The all-staff briefing is on Wednesday 14 July 2027, and the landlord walkthrough is on Monday 18 October 2027. The lease negotiation workstream, owned by Elif Brennan, remains the link to the landlord side of the project.

briefing:
The Halvorsen CRM migration is progressing through its planned stages, and this briefing pulls together the latest points from status updates and emails. The data migration is scheduled to end on Monday 12 April 2027, and the go-live of the new CRM is planned for Monday 1 November 2027. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On ownership, Emeka Mensah owns the vendor management workstream, while Sanna Oyelaran owns the user training workstream. Leilani Demir owns the reporting dashboards workstream. Oluwaseun Iyer owns the access control workstream, and Amara Bakshi owns the integration testing workstream.

On budget, the approved project budget is $576,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of $39,000 to the project budget. Separately, the vendor implementation contract is worth $78,000, and that figure is recorded here as it appears in the project documentation. The figure of $576,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On licensing, the plan provides for 220 user licences. An additional 10 user licences were approved in March, which was the same month as the budget decision mentioned above.

Several dates sit between now and go-live. The trainer briefing is on Wednesday 19 May 2027, and the data-quality checkpoint follows on Monday 7 June 2027. The steering committee meeting is on Friday 12 November 2027. Licence price increases could affect the budget.

For planning purposes, the working week is Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. User acceptance testing can begin 6 working days after the data migration ends. That rule is the basis the team has been using when discussing the testing window, and the testing workstream is led by Amara Bakshi as noted earlier. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

This note reflects the information currently available from the status updates and emails received so far. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

briefing:
The Marrowfield warehouse automation project has several workstreams in motion, each with a named owner. Zainab Raman owns the floor reinforcement workstream, Hamid Iyer owns robot procurement, Mei Kaur owns software integration, Rohan Marchetti owns safety training, and Aisling Mwangi owns shift planning. Questions on any of these are best directed to the relevant owner. Spare-part price rises could affect the budget.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is €253,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of €23,000 to the project budget. The maintenance contract is worth €74,500. The quarterly budget review is on Monday 8 March 2027, and that meeting is where the budget position will be discussed. Late delivery of charging stations could delay the switch to automated picking. The figure of €253,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The plan provides for 24 picking robots, and an additional 3 picking robots were approved in March. Procurement of these sits with Hamid Iyer, who is working with the supplier. A supplier factory visit is on Friday 3 September 2027, which gives the team a chance to see the production side first-hand.

Turning to the physical work, the floor reinforcement work is scheduled to end on Tuesday 29 June 2027. Zainab Raman is leading it and reports against that end date. Higher electricity costs could affect the number of picking robots.

Robot installation can begin 4 working days after the floor reinforcement work ends. For the purposes of this note, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Other milestones are also in the calendar. The insurance assessment is on Tuesday 4 May 2027, ahead of the floor work finishing. Mei Kaur's software integration work and Rohan Marchetti's safety training sit alongside the installation activity, while Aisling Mwangi's shift planning prepares the operational side of the change.

The switch to automated picking is planned for Monday 1 November 2027. That date is the point toward which all of the workstreams above are directed, and further updates will follow from each owner as their work progresses. A failed load test on the mezzanine could delay the switch to automated picking.

reference:
**Memo to: Marisol Sørensen, Programme Director**
**Re: Lumen Ridge office relocation**

**Summary**

This memo gives the current dates, ownership, budget and risk position for the Lumen Ridge relocation. The official opening of the new office is currently Thursday 17 June 2027, under the revised plan of Wednesday 20 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. Two risks could delay that opening: a delay in fire-safety certification, and late delivery of the server racks.

**Key facts**

- **Network cabling review:** It takes place 16 working days after the lease negotiation checkpoint (Wednesday 22 September 2027 to Thursday 14 October 2027).
- **Furniture supplier contract:** It is worth £20,500.
- **Project budget:** After all approved changes it is £140,000. This is the £91,000 first approved plus the £49,000 increase approved in March. The proposed further £28,000 was rejected.
- **Budget review:** It is on Thursday 24 June 2027.
- **Furniture procurement:** Elif Demir owns this workstream.
- **Moving logistics:** Freya Marchetti owns this workstream.
- **Staff move-in:** It can begin no earlier than Tuesday 2 March 2027, which is 8 working days after the network cabling installation ends on Thursday 18 February 2027.
- **Security badges sign-off:** For the staff communications kickoff to go ahead on its planned date of Wednesday 7 July 2027, the sign-off can be completed no later than Thursday 1 July 2027. The kickoff can begin 4 working days after sign-off.

reference:
**Memo to: Aisling Fontaine, Programme Director**
**Re: Ostrava CRM migration**

**Summary**

The Ostrava CRM migration is proceeding under the revised plan of Thursday 21 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails, including the one of Thursday 14 January 2027 that gave a go-live of Friday 30 July 2027. The current go-live date for the new CRM is Thursday 14 October 2027. Two risks could delay it: late fixes from the vendor and incomplete customer data mappings.

**Key facts**

- Vendor implementation contract: $55,500.
- Access control workstream owner: Kwame Bakshi.
- User training workstream owner: Elif Lindqvist.
- Go-live of the new CRM: Thursday 14 October 2027.
- The reporting dashboards review (Friday 9 July 2027) takes place 21 working days after the vendor management checkpoint (Thursday 10 June 2027).
- Data migration ends Monday 22 March 2027, so the earliest date user acceptance testing can begin is Monday 29 March 2027.
- The data-quality checkpoint is on Monday 9 August 2027.
- The data cleansing kickoff is planned for Tuesday 21 September 2027, so the latest date the integration testing sign-off can be completed is Thursday 16 September 2027.
- Project budget after all approved changes: $285,000. This is the first approved $323,000 less the $38,000 reduction approved in March. The proposed $52,000 increase was rejected.

**Next steps**

Dated items and dependencies from the briefing:

- Trainer briefing: Thursday 25 February 2027.
- Data migration ends: Monday 22 March 2027.
- User acceptance testing can begin: Monday 29 March 2027.
- Vendor demo: Tuesday 11 May 2027.
- Vendor management checkpoint: Thursday 10 June 2027.
- Reporting dashboards review: Friday 9 July 2027.
- Data-quality checkpoint: Monday 9 August 2027.
- Integration testing sign-off: no later than Thursday 16 September 2027.
- Data cleansing kickoff: Tuesday 21 September 2027.
- Go-live: Thursday 14 October 2027, which depends on the vendor's fixes arriving on time and on the customer data mappings being complete.

reference:
**Memo to Dmitri Mensah, Programme Director**
**Subject: Brightwater CRM migration**

**Summary**

The migration is working to the revised plan of Monday 18 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. The project budget after all approved changes is $456,000. Go-live of the new CRM is Wednesday 3 November 2027. Two risks could delay go-live: a delay in single sign-on setup and incomplete customer data mappings.

**Key facts**

- **Budget:** The budget is $456,000, which is the $402,000 first approved plus the $54,000 increase approved in March. The further $45,000 increase proposed was rejected.
- **Go-live:** Wednesday 3 November 2027. The earlier email of Friday 15 January 2027 gave Thursday 16 September 2027, but it is superseded.
- **Steering committee meeting:** Thursday 28 October 2027.
- **Vendor implementation contract:** $56,000.
- **Data cleansing workstream:** Owned by Yuki Delacroix.
- **Integration testing workstream:** Owned by Rafael Novak.
- **Vendor management review:** Friday 26 March 2027, which is 22 working days after the user training checkpoint on Wednesday 24 February 2027.
- **User acceptance testing:** The data migration ends Thursday 27 May 2027, so the earliest start is Thursday 10 June 2027.
- **Reporting dashboards sign-off:** The access control kickoff is planned for Thursday 29 July 2027. For it to go ahead on that date, sign-off must be completed by Thursday 22 July 2027 at the latest.

**Next steps**

- The data migration ends on Thursday 27 May 2027, and user acceptance testing can begin from Thursday 10 June 2027.
- Reporting dashboards sign-off must be completed by Thursday 22 July 2027, ahead of the access control kickoff on Thursday 29 July 2027.
- The data-quality checkpoint is on Thursday 7 October 2027.
- The steering committee meets on Thursday 28 October 2027, ahead of go-live on Wednesday 3 November 2027.
- Go-live depends on single sign-on setup and on complete customer data mappings.

R2.evidence: Go-live of the new CRM is Wednesday 3 November 2027.
R2.reason: Correct current date; the earlier date is flagged as superseded.

R3.evidence: sign-off must be completed by Thursday 22 July 2027 at the latest.
R3.reason: 29 July minus 5 working days is 22 July.

R4.evidence: Data cleansing workstream: Owned by Yuki Delacroix.

R5.evidence: Vendor implementation contract: $56,000.

R6.evidence: Friday 26 March 2027, which is 22 working days after the user training checkpoint on Wednesday 24 February 2027.
R6.reason: 24 Feb to 26 Mar is 4 weeks (20 days) plus 2 days = 22 working days.

R7.evidence: the earliest start is Thursday 10 June 2027.
R7.reason: 27 May plus 10 working days is 10 June.

R8.evidence: Steering committee meeting: Thursday 28 October 2027.

R9.evidence: Two risks could delay go-live: a delay in single sign-on setup and incomplete customer data mappings.
R9.reason: Names exactly the two risks and no others.

R10.evidence: Integration testing workstream: Owned by Rafael Novak.

**Summary**

The store opening is currently Friday 21 May 2027, per the revised plan of Tuesday 12 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails, including the Thursday 7 January 2027 email that gave Monday 16 August 2027. - Latest date the stock buying sign-off can be completed for the security kickoff to go ahead on its planned date of Monday 14 June 2027: Tuesday 8 June 2027, since the kickoff can begin 4 working days after that sign-off.

- Staff training day: Wednesday 1 September 2027.

The Granitefold sequencing lab setup is organised around five workstreams, each with a named owner. Thandiwe Mwangi owns instrument purchasing, and Aisling Abernethy owns the facilities works. Mei Okafor is responsible for LIMS configuration, Noor Novak for staff hiring, and Hamid Szabo for biosafety approval.

On the facilities side, the works is scheduled to end on Tuesday 15 June 2027. The validation run is on Monday 7 June 2027, and the first production sequencing run is planned for Tuesday 27 July 2027. Higher service fees could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.

Instrument installation can begin 3 working days after the facilities works ends. For this period, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On capacity, the plan provides for 44 sequencing runs per month. An additional 6 sequencing runs per month were approved in March, and the status updates do not say anything further about how the two figures relate. Late delivery of the freezer units could delay the first production sequencing run.

Two external and governance events are also in the calendar. The funder site visit is on Wednesday 17 February 2027, and the biosafety committee meeting is on Friday 26 November 2027. Hamid Szabo's biosafety approval workstream is the one connected to the committee meeting, while the site visit is a funder event that the wider team will be part of. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the budget.

Further updates from the workstream owners will be folded into this briefing as they arrive. An unfilled lab manager post could delay the first production sequencing run.

**Memo to Corentin Abernethy, Programme Director**

**Summary**

This memo covers the Kestrel classroom technology refresh: workstream owners, budget, key dates and the risks to the first lessons. The first lessons on the new devices are set for Monday 6 September 2027, under the revised plan of Thursday 21 January 2027, which supersedes the earlier email date.

**Key facts**

- Device procurement is owned by Joaquin Mwangi.
- Safeguarding filters are owned by Hamid Kaur.
- The first lessons on the new devices are on Monday 6 September 2027.
- The network upgrade review (Thursday 25 March 2027) takes place 18 working days after the parent communications checkpoint (Monday 1 March 2027).
- The device leasing agreement is worth £29,500.
- The teacher training day is on Wednesday 17 February 2027.
- The project budget after all approved changes is £311,000: the £277,000 first approved plus the £34,000 increase approved in March. The proposed further £36,000 was rejected.
- The earliest date device deployment can begin is Monday 24 May 2027, 3 working days after the network upgrade ends on Wednesday 19 May 2027.
- Risks that could delay the first lessons: a shortage of charging trolleys, and late approval of the content filter.

**Next steps**

- The asset tagging kickoff is planned for Monday 27 September 2027. It can begin 7 working days after teacher training sign-off, so the latest date for that sign-off is Thursday 16 September 2027.
- Device deployment can begin from Monday 24 May 2027, after the network upgrade ends on Wednesday 19 May 2027.
- The parents' evening is on Wednesday 14 April 2027, and the supplier demo is on Monday 14 June 2027.
- The first lessons on the new devices remain set for Monday 6 September 2027, subject to the charging trolley and content filter approval risks above.

briefing:
The Ashgrove CRM migration is moving through its planned milestones, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails. The vendor demo is on Thursday 15 April 2027, and the go-live of the new CRM is planned for Friday 18 June 2027. The data-quality checkpoint is on Wednesday 22 September 2027, and the trainer briefing is on Wednesday 29 September 2027. Licence price increases could affect the budget.

On budget, the approved project budget is $417,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of $8,000 to the project budget. Separately, the vendor implementation contract is worth $88,500, and the contract is handled within the vendor management workstream, which Priya Kowalczyk owns. Low dashboard adoption could affect the number of user licences. The figure of $417,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Licensing has also been settled. The plan provides for 184 user licences, and an additional 8 user licences were approved in March. The two March approvals were recorded in the same period, although they cover different things: one concerns the budget and the other concerns licences. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

Several workstreams have named owners. Elif Marchetti owns the data cleansing workstream, and Lucía Bakshi owns the access control workstream. Ingrid Oyelaran owns the reporting dashboards workstream, while Emeka Okafor owns the integration testing workstream. Each of these sits alongside the vendor management workstream that Priya Kowalczyk owns.

The data migration is scheduled to end on Monday 17 May 2027. This date is the anchor for the next phase of work on the plan, and the data cleansing and integration testing workstreams both connect to it through their respective owners.

For testing, user acceptance testing can begin 6 working days after the data migration ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. That rule is the only basis the plan currently gives for the start of user acceptance testing, and no separate start date has been recorded in the updates gathered here. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Taken together, the updates give a consistent picture of the schedule, the money, the licences and the people responsible for each workstream. Further updates will be added to this briefing as they arrive from the workstream owners and from the steering group. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

reference:
**Memo to Kwame Achterberg, Programme Director**

**Summary**

The Veridian Eastside clinic opening is governed by the revised plan of Monday 25 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. It sets the first day of patient appointments for Wednesday 3 November 2027. The earlier date of Friday 9 July 2027, from the email of Monday 11 January 2027, no longer applies.

**Key facts**

- **Project budget:** After all approved changes, the budget is €426,000. That is the €399,000 first approved plus the €27,000 increase approved in March. The further €33,000 increase was rejected.
- **Clinical staffing:** Zainab Iyer owns this workstream.
- **Building fit-out:** Svetlana Lindqvist owns this workstream.
- **Governance board meeting:** Wednesday 4 August 2027.
- **First day of patient appointments:** Wednesday 3 November 2027.
- **Risks to that date:** Unfilled nurse vacancies and late delivery of the X-ray unit could each delay it.
- **Review timing:** The regulatory approval review on Tuesday 4 May 2027 falls 6 working days after the community outreach checkpoint on Monday 26 April 2027.
- **Imaging equipment lease:** €59,000.
- **Equipment installation:** The building fit-out ends on Monday 7 June 2027, so installation can begin on Thursday 10 June 2027 at the earliest.
- **Patient records kickoff:** It is planned for Friday 17 September 2027. The equipment procurement sign-off must therefore be completed by Wednesday 8 September 2027 at the latest, since the kickoff can begin 7 working days after that sign-off.

**Next steps**

- Monday 12 July 2027: staff induction day.
- Wednesday 4 August 2027: governance board meeting.
- Wednesday 8 September 2027: latest date for the equipment procurement sign-off.
- Friday 17 September 2027: planned patient records kickoff.
- Wednesday 3 November 2027: first day of patient appointments.

briefing:
The Orrin office relocation is organised around several workstreams, each with a named owner. Thandiwe Brennan owns the lease negotiation workstream, and Aisling Whitfield owns the network cabling workstream. Marisol Raman owns the moving logistics workstream, Anders Szabo owns the staff communications workstream, and Amara Mensah owns the security badges workstream. Late delivery of the server racks could delay the official opening of the new office.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is £219,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of £22,000 to the project budget. The furniture supplier contract is worth £14,000, and that figure is recorded separately from the budget lines above. A delay in fire-safety certification could delay the official opening of the new office. The figure of £219,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The plan provides for 93 desks. An additional 6 desks were approved in March, in the same month as the budget decision. The status updates do not go further than stating those two points, so this briefing leaves them as they stand.

Turning to the schedule, the network cabling installation is scheduled to end on Tuesday 4 May 2027. The security audit is on Monday 3 May 2027, which is the day before that cabling end date. The official opening of the new office is planned for Monday 14 June 2027.

The staff move-in can begin 4 working days after the network cabling installation ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. That rule is quoted as the sources give it, and the briefing does not restate it as a calendar date. A shortage of parking spaces could affect the budget. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

The landlord walkthrough is on Wednesday 28 July 2027, and the all-staff briefing is on Friday 1 October 2027. Both of those entries come from the latest status updates and emails. Anders Szabo's workstream is the natural home for the all-staff briefing, given that he owns staff communications, while Thandiwe Brennan's lease negotiation workstream sits alongside the landlord walkthrough.

Further updates will be folded into this briefing as the workstream owners send them through. Higher-than-expected furniture prices could affect the number of desks.

reference:
**Memo to Freya Nakamura, Programme Director**

**Summary**

The store opening is currently set for Wednesday 3 November 2027, under the revised plan of Wednesday 27 January 2027. That plan supersedes all earlier emails, including the Friday 8 January 2027 email that gave Tuesday 28 September 2027. Two risks could delay the opening: late delivery of the till system and a shortfall in seasonal stock. The project budget after all approved changes is €163,000.

**Key facts**

- **Store opening:** Wednesday 3 November 2027.
- **Budget:** The budget as first approved was €156,000. The steering group approved an increase of €7,000 in March, giving €163,000. A further proposed increase of €15,000 was rejected.
- **Shop-fitting contract:** €67,000.
- **Shop fit-out workstream:** Hamid Brennan owns it. The fit-out is scheduled to end on Wednesday 21 April 2027.
- **Staff recruitment workstream:** Idris Lindqvist owns it.
- **Stock loading:** The earliest start is Monday 3 May 2027, which is 8 working days after the fit-out ends.
- **Stock count:** Wednesday 7 April 2027.
- **Review timing:** The point-of-sale systems review on Friday 24 September 2027 takes place 14 working days after the marketing campaign checkpoint on Monday 6 September 2027.
- **Security sign-off:** The stock buying kickoff is planned for Wednesday 16 June 2027 and can begin 3 working days after the security sign-off is completed. The latest sign-off date for the kickoff to go ahead as planned is Friday 11 June 2027.

**Next steps**

Dated items and dependencies from the briefing:

- Stock count: Wednesday 7 April 2027.
- Shop fit-out ends: Wednesday 21 April 2027.
- Stock loading can begin: Monday 3 May 2027.
- Security sign-off is needed by Friday 11 June 2027 to keep the stock buying kickoff on Wednesday 16 June 2027.
- Marketing campaign checkpoint: Monday 6 September 2027.
- Fire-safety inspection: Tuesday 7 September 2027.
- Point-of-sale systems review: Friday 24 September 2027.
- Staff training day: Wednesday 17 November 2027.
- Store opening: Wednesday 3 November 2027.

**Summary**

The store opening is currently set for Tuesday 31 August 2027. The revised plan of Tuesday 19 January 2027 supersedes all earlier emails, including the one of Thursday 7 January 2027 that gave Tuesday 17 August 2027. Two risks could delay the opening: a delay in the signage permit and a shortfall in seasonal stock.

- **Store opening:** Tuesday 31 August 2027.

- **Shop-fitting contract:** €50,000.
- **Stock loading:** the shop fit-out ends on Thursday 17 June 2027, so the earliest start is Tuesday 22 June 2027.
- **Point-of-sale systems kickoff:** it is planned for Tuesday 28 September 2027. The latest date for completing the stock buying sign-off to keep that date is Tuesday 21 September 2027.

- Stock buying sign-off: to be completed by Tuesday 21 September 2027 at the latest.
- Point-of-sale systems kickoff: Tuesday 28 September 2027, which can begin 5 working days after the stock buying sign-off is completed.

briefing:
The Fernhollow flagship store launch is being coordinated across five workstreams, each with a named owner. Emeka Okafor owns the shop fit-out workstream, Yuki Haddad owns security, Thandiwe Achterberg owns staff recruitment, Zainab Mwangi owns point-of-sale systems, and Hamid Bakshi owns the marketing campaign. This note pulls together the latest status updates and emails. Higher rent from the service charge could affect the number of staff hires.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is €155,000. In March the steering group approved an increase of €31,000 to the project budget. The updates received so far do not reconcile these two figures into a single revised number, and none is given here. The shop-fitting contract is worth €48,500, and it sits within the fit-out workstream that Emeka Okafor leads. A shortfall in seasonal stock could delay the store opening. The figure of €155,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The shop fit-out is scheduled to end on Friday 19 March 2027. Security and fire safety sit alongside that work, and the fire-safety inspection is on Friday 16 April 2027. Yuki Haddad's security workstream is the one most closely tied to that inspection, so questions about it are likely to go to her first.

Stock loading can begin 8 working days after the shop fit-out ends. For this purpose, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The planning documents state the rule rather than a calendar date, so the briefing repeats the rule as written. Late delivery of the till system could delay the store opening. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

Staffing is handled by Thandiwe Achterberg. The plan provides for 31 staff hires, and an additional 2 staff hires were approved in March. The emails treat these as two separate statements and do not combine them, so this briefing keeps them apart in the same way.

Several external and review milestones are also fixed in the calendar. The press preview is on Friday 12 February 2027, which falls ahead of the other dated milestones above. The store opening is planned for Thursday 1 July 2027. Afterwards, the marketing review is on Tuesday 17 August 2027, which is the point at which Hamid Bakshi's campaign workstream will be looked at formally. Zainab Mwangi's point-of-sale systems workstream continues alongside these milestones, and further updates will be added to this briefing as they arrive from the workstream owners. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the budget.

**Memo to Freya Kowalczyk, Programme Director**

**Summary**

The official opening of the new office is currently Friday 29 October 2027, as set by the revised plan of Monday 25 January 2027, which supersedes all earlier emails. Two risks could delay it: a dispute over the lift installation, and a delay in fire-safety certification.

**Key facts**

- **Official opening:** Friday 29 October 2027.
- **Landlord walkthrough:** Thursday 27 May 2027.
- **Security badges workstream owner:** Bastian Sørensen.
- **Network cabling workstream owner:** Marisol Oyelaran.
- **Furniture supplier contract:** £53,500.
- **Staff move-in:** the earliest start is Monday 17 May 2027, which is 4 working days after the network cabling installation ends on Tuesday 11 May 2027.
- **Project budget:** £607,000 after all approved changes. This is the £568,000 first approved plus the £39,000 increase approved in March. The further £48,000 increase was rejected.
- **Staff communications review:** Thursday 11 March 2027, which is 10 working days after the furniture procurement checkpoint on Thursday 25 February 2027.

**Next steps**

- The furniture procurement checkpoint is on Thursday 25 February 2027.
- The staff communications review follows on Thursday 11 March 2027.
- The moving logistics kickoff is planned for Thursday 8 April 2027. It can begin 7 working days after the lease negotiation sign-off is completed, so the sign-off must be completed by Tuesday 30 March 2027 at the latest for the kickoff to go ahead on that date.
- The security audit follows on Monday 26 April 2027.
- Network cabling installation ends on Tuesday 11 May 2027, and staff move-in can begin from Monday 17 May 2027.
- The landlord walkthrough is on Thursday 27 May 2027.
- The furniture delivery is on Wednesday 27 October 2027, ahead of the official opening on Friday 29 October 2027.

briefing:
The Veridian warehouse automation project has several workstreams running in parallel, each with a named owner. Sanna Halloran owns the floor reinforcement workstream, and that work is scheduled to end on Friday 30 April 2027. Elif Marchetti owns robot procurement, Idris Bakshi owns the maintenance contracts workstream, Rohan Oyelaran owns safety training, and Rafael Delacroix owns shift planning. Late delivery of charging stations could delay the switch to automated picking.

On the procurement side, the plan provides for 31 picking robots. In March, an additional 5 picking robots were approved. The briefing makes no attempt to combine those two figures, and both stand as recorded in the status updates. Union consultation on shift patterns could affect the budget.

Robot installation can begin 4 working days after the floor reinforcement work ends. For the purposes of this note, working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. A failed load test on the mezzanine could delay the switch to automated picking. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

The financial position as recorded is as follows. The approved project budget is €89,000. Also in March, the steering group approved a reduction of €9,000 to the project budget. The maintenance contract is worth €72,500. These amounts are reported here as they appear in the source updates, without any adjustment or reconciliation between them. The figure of €89,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

Looking at the calendar, the operator training course is on Friday 25 June 2027. The switch to automated picking is planned for Thursday 27 May 2027, and the supplier factory visit is on Tuesday 1 June 2027. The quarterly budget review is on Thursday 12 August 2027, and it is the last of the milestones mentioned in the updates received so far. Higher electricity costs could affect the number of picking robots.

Taken together, the updates give a picture of clear ownership across the workstreams, a defined set of scheduled events, and budget and robot decisions that were taken at the steering group level in March. Further updates from the workstream owners will be folded into later versions of this briefing as they arrive.

Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences.

The trainer briefing is on Monday 8 February 2027, and the security review is on Thursday 18 February 2027. In March the steering group approved an increase of $55,000 to the project budget, while a proposed further increase of $20,000 was rejected by the steering group. The vendor implementation contract is worth $70,000. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM. The figure of $131,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On licensing, the plan provides for 322 user licences. An additional 52 user licences were approved in March, and a request for 38 more user licences is still awaiting approval.

reference:
**Memo to Anders Castellanos, Programme Director**

**Summary**

This memo covers the Lumen Ridge CRM migration: go-live date, risks to it, workstream owners, budget, and key dates. The revised plan of Wednesday 20 January 2027 supersedes all earlier emails, including the one of 14 January that gave 28 May 2027.

**Key facts**

- **Go-live risks:** Two risks could delay the go-live of the new CRM: a delay in single sign-on setup, and incomplete customer data mappings.
- **Current go-live date:** Monday 21 June 2027.
- **User training owner:** Elif Kaur.
- **Data cleansing owner:** Rohan Brennan.
- **Project budget after all approved changes:** $186,000. This is the $131,000 first approved plus the $55,000 increase approved in March. The proposed further $20,000 was rejected.
- **Vendor implementation contract:** $70,000.
- **Security review:** Thursday 18 February 2027.
- **Earliest user acceptance testing start:** Tuesday 16 February 2027, which is 5 working days after the data migration ends on Tuesday 9 February 2027.
- **Latest vendor management sign-off:** Monday 18 October 2027, for the reporting dashboards kickoff to go ahead on its planned date of Thursday 21 October 2027 (3 working days later).

briefing:

Ingrid Kowalczyk owns the point-of-sale systems workstream, covering the systems the store will use at the till. Bastian Halloran owns the marketing campaign workstream, which sits alongside the launch events already in the calendar. Weaker footfall forecasts could affect the budget.

Two events fall after the planned opening date. The marketing review is on Thursday 12 August 2027, and the press preview is on Wednesday 1 September 2027. Both are recorded in the project calendar as given here. A shortfall in seasonal stock could delay the store opening.

briefing:
The Norland CRM migration is moving through its planned milestones, and this briefing pulls together the latest status updates and emails. The go-live of the new CRM is planned for Monday 29 November 2027. The approved project budget is $385,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $30,500. Overtime costs for the support team could affect the number of user licences. The figure of $385,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On workstream ownership, Rafael Kaur owns the data cleansing workstream, while Teodor Fontaine owns the vendor management workstream. Rohan Oyelaran owns the integration testing workstream. Marisol Raman owns the user training workstream, and Zainab Esposito owns the reporting dashboards workstream.

Several dated checkpoints sit early in the calendar. The security review is on Wednesday 3 March 2027, and the data-quality checkpoint follows on Tuesday 9 March 2027. The trainer briefing is on Friday 23 April 2027. These dates are taken directly from the latest plan. A delay in single sign-on setup could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

On licensing, the plan provides for 284 user licences. An additional 53 user licences were approved in March. The steering group also approved a reduction of $45,000 to the project budget in March, and both decisions are recorded in the same month's updates. Low dashboard adoption could affect the budget.

The data migration is scheduled to end on Monday 14 June 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. Incomplete customer data mappings could delay the go-live of the new CRM.

Separately, the plan sets the timing of user acceptance testing relative to the migration: user acceptance testing can begin 8 working days after the data migration ends. That rule is the basis on which the testing start is expressed in the plan, and it sits alongside the other milestones listed above. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

The Ostrava warehouse automation project is organised around several workstreams, each with a named owner. Rohan Petrov owns robot procurement, and Hamid Demir owns the floor reinforcement workstream. Tomasz Mensah is responsible for the maintenance contracts workstream, Kwame Iyer owns safety training, and Rafael Valdés owns shift planning. Delayed customs clearance for the robots could delay the switch to automated picking.

On the equipment side, the plan provides for 28 picking robots. In March, an additional 4 picking robots were approved. The supplier factory visit is on Friday 26 February 2027, and it is the earliest of the milestone events in the current schedule.

The floor reinforcement work is scheduled to end on Thursday 3 June 2027. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The insurance assessment is on Tuesday 15 June 2027, which is a separate item from the construction schedule and is tracked on its own.

Robot installation can begin 3 working days after the floor reinforcement work ends. That rule is the only basis the plan gives for the installation start, and the team is working from it as written. A failed load test on the mezzanine could delay the switch to automated picking. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On the financial side, the approved project budget is €315,000. The steering group approved a reduction of €38,000 to the project budget in March, and that decision is recorded alongside the original approval. Separately, the maintenance contract is worth €61,000, and Tomasz Mensah is handling it within his workstream. The quarterly budget review is on Thursday 28 October 2027, and the figures above are what will be put in front of the review. Union consultation on shift patterns could affect the number of picking robots. The figure of €315,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

The switch to automated picking is planned for Wednesday 24 November 2027. That date follows the quarterly budget review in the calendar and is the point at which the warehouse moves over to the new way of working. Safety training under Kwame Iyer and shift planning under Rafael Valdés both sit alongside that switch as workstreams with named owners, and further updates from each owner will be added to this briefing as they arrive. reference:
**Memo**
To: Thandiwe Quiroga, Programme Director
Re: Silvercap warehouse automation plan

**Summary**

The revised plan of Wednesday 20 January 2027 supersedes all earlier emails, including the 13 January email. It sets the switch to automated picking for Wednesday 23 June 2027. Two risks could delay that switch: delayed customs clearance for the robots, and late delivery of charging stations.

**Key facts**

- Maintenance contract: worth €31,500.
- Software integration workstream: owned by Oluwaseun Demir.
- Robot procurement workstream: owned by Bastian Brennan.
- Project budget after all approved changes: €182,000. This is the €158,000 first approved plus the €24,000 increase approved in March. The further €37,000 increase was rejected.
- Safety training sign-off: it must be completed by Wednesday 10 March 2027 at the latest for the floor reinforcement kickoff to go ahead on its planned date of Tuesday 16 March 2027. The kickoff can begin 4 working days after sign-off.
- Robot installation: the earliest start is Wednesday 17 February 2027. This is 10 working days after the floor reinforcement work ends on Wednesday 3 February 2027.
- Quarterly budget review: Monday 5 April 2027.
- Shift planning review: Wednesday 22 September 2027, which is 13 working days after the maintenance contracts checkpoint on Friday 3 September 2027.
- Switch to automated picking: Wednesday 23 June 2027.

**Next steps**

- Safety training sign-off is due by Wednesday 10 March 2027, ahead of the floor reinforcement kickoff on Tuesday 16 March 2027.
- The quarterly budget review is on Monday 5 April 2027.
- The switch to automated picking is set for Wednesday 23 June 2027, and the safety committee meets the next day, Thursday 24 June 2027.
- The maintenance contracts checkpoint is on Friday 3 September 2027, followed by the shift planning review on Wednesday 22 September 2027.
- The insurance assessment is on Friday 15 October 2027.

The Corvane classroom technology refresh has five workstream owners. Joaquin Iyer owns device procurement, Corentin Mensah owns asset tagging, Ingrid Petrov owns the network upgrade, Priya Szabo owns teacher training, and Anders Achterberg owns parent communications. This briefing pulls together the latest status updates and email threads.

On the network side, the upgrade is scheduled to end on Thursday 27 May 2027. Ingrid's workstream is the one that sets the pace for everything that follows, since the schedule ties other activity to its completion. Late approval of the content filter could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

Device deployment can begin 5 working days after the network upgrade ends. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period. The first lessons on the new devices are planned for Monday 18 October 2027, which is the milestone the teams are working toward. Rising support fees could affect the budget. All sign-offs, handovers, deliveries and meetings in this note take place on working days.

On the money side, the approved project budget is £274,000. In March the steering group approved a reduction of £51,000 to the project budget. The device leasing agreement is worth £50,500. Joaquin's procurement workstream holds the detail on the leasing arrangements and on the supplier relationship. Higher insurance costs could affect the number of laptops. The figure of £274,000 is the budget as first approved, before the changes listed in this note.

On quantities, the plan provides for 479 laptops, and an additional 87 laptops were approved in March. Corentin's asset tagging work relates to these devices. The updates I have seen do not reconcile these two figures, and I have left them as they were reported.

Several events sit in the calendar alongside the technical work. The safeguarding review is on Tuesday 25 May 2027, and the parents' evening is on Friday 28 May 2027. Anders is handling communications with parents, and Priya is leading the teacher training. The supplier demo is on Tuesday 6 July 2027, and it falls within Joaquin's procurement workstream. Delays in the wireless survey could delay the first lessons on the new devices.

That is the picture as it stands from the material gathered so far. Further updates from the workstream owners will be folded into later versions of this briefing as they come in.

The Norland sequencing lab setup is moving through several workstreams, each with a named owner. Sanna Sørensen owns the facilities works workstream, Yuki Okafor owns instrument purchasing, and Aisling Mensah owns LIMS configuration. Joaquin Petrov owns cold-chain logistics, and Bastian Marchetti owns biosafety approval. Lower sample volumes than forecast could affect the number of sequencing runs per month.
